title: Screen 2: Wave — non-blocking review follow-ups
description: Non-blocking findings from pr-reviewer's review of PR #21 (screen2-wave), tracked here per CLAUDE.md's autonomous-pipeline rule so they aren't lost once that PR merges. None are blocking; pick up if this area is touched again or as standalone cleanup.

checklist.step: _is_force_index_spike's `negative: bool` parameter forces double-negative reasoning (`if negative and latest >= 0`, `if not negative and latest <= 0`); both branches are correct and tested, but a signed-multiplier form would read more directly for a future editor.

Fix the self-contradictory docstring on evaluate_wave's new len-guard: it says it mirrors evaluate_impulse's `len(daily_ohlcv) < 2` guard 'in this same module (app/signals/impulse.py)', but evaluate_wave lives in triple_screen.py, a different module, and the condition actually implemented is `== 0`, not `< 2`.

Add a regression test pinning the 1-row daily_ohlcv boundary case — only 0 rows is currently covered (test_empty_daily_ohlcv_degrades_to_no_wave_instead_of_raising); the 0-row-vs-<2 guard asymmetry vs. evaluate_impulse means a future stricter single-row check elsewhere wouldn't be caught here.

decisions.decision: Replaced _is_force_index_spike's `if negative and latest >= 0: return False` / `if not negative and latest <= 0: return False` pair with a single `sign = -1 if negative else 1; if sign * latest <= 0: return False`, keeping the existing `negative: bool` keyword-only parameter (and all existing call sites/tests) unchanged rather than renaming it to a signed multiplier itself.
decisions.rationale: The checklist item's own wording ('a signed-multiplier form would read more directly') is about the internal reasoning, not the public parameter name; `_is_force_index_spike(..., negative=True)` at each call site (evaluate_wave's two branches) already reads clearly as 'is this a negative spike', and renaming the parameter would touch call sites and tests for no behavior or readability gain. The one-line signed-multiplier check removes the double-negative (`not negative and ...`) branch entirely while staying provably equivalent (sign=-1 -> sign*latest<=0 == latest>=0; sign=1 -> sign*latest<=0 == latest<=0), and all existing TestIsForceIndexSpike cases plus the two end-to-end Wave tests pass unchanged, confirming no behavior drift.

decisions.decision: Rewrote evaluate_wave's len-guard docstring paragraph to name the correct module (app/signals/impulse.py, explicitly called out as a different module from this one) and to explain *why* the guard here is `== 0` rather than evaluate_impulse's `< 2` (this function only ever reads `.iloc[-1]`, never `.iloc[-2]`, and stochastic_oscillator/force_index already return NaN rather than raise for a 1-row input) instead of just asserting mirrored behavior.
decisions.rationale: The old text was self-contradictory (claimed impulse.py was 'this same module' while evaluate_wave lives in triple_screen.py) and imprecise (claimed the guard mirrors `< 2` when the code implements `== 0`). Explaining the actual reason for the asymmetry (fewer required rows because the two indicators tolerate a 1-row input) is more useful to a future editor than just restating the numbers, and is now backed by test_single_row_daily_ohlcv_degrades_to_no_wave_instead_of_raising.

decisions.decision: Added test_single_row_daily_ohlcv_degrades_to_no_wave_instead_of_raising using real (unmocked) stochastic_oscillator/force_index, mirroring the existing 0-row test's unmocked style, rather than mocking stochastic_k/force_index_2ema to NaN directly.
decisions.rationale: The point of this regression test is specifically to prove the 1-row boundary doesn't need its own guard because the underlying indicators already degrade to NaN for insufficient history and .iloc[-1] on a 1-element Series doesn't raise; mocking the indicators' outputs to NaN would only test the already-covered 'NaN input produces NO_WAVE' path (test_nan_stochastic_k_from_insufficient_history_is_no_wave) and wouldn't catch a future stricter single-row check inside either indicator, which is exactly the gap the checklist item flagged.
